meaning.evidence: All decisions, rates, dates and votes kept; the quoted directive and statement left verbatim, as quotations should be. Small shifts: "doubled down on the FOMC's policy" for reaffirmed and "still running too hot" for elevated relative to the goal; "a bit quicker" for timelier.

sense.evidence: Most fit: "bump the target range ... up", "hadn't budged much", "dead set on hitting", "The meeting knocked off at 10:15 a.m.", "voted as one". "doubled down" carries a risk-raising sense reaffirmed doesn't have.

authenticity.evidence: Mostly natural Aussie ("When the yakking wrapped up", "next get-together", "knocked off"), with "doubled down" an Americanism and "the whole lot of members" a clunky stock phrase.

register.evidence: A full level-4 retelling of the narrative, quotes untouched; "Not a single bugger." is within vulgarity 1.

tone.evidence: The formal minutes become a matey account, as a level-4 retelling should; the gravity of the rate decision survives ("made it crystal clear it's still dead set on hitting its dual-mandate goals").

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly, though "the whole lot of members agreed to bump the target range for the federal funds rate up 1/4 percentage point" is a little awkward.

variety.evidence: Varied: "bump", "lift", "doubled down", "hadn't budged", "yakking", "sign off", "voted as one", "get-together", "knocked off", "thumbs-up"; "sign off" twice.

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the FOMC policy-actions minutes, structure and quoted texts intact.

problems.quote: doubled down on the FOMC's policy
problems.why: Doubled down is American and implies escalation rather than restatement.

problems.quote: the whole lot of members agreed
problems.why: Clunky; reads as a forced swap.

problems.quote: inflation was still running too hot
problems.original: inflation remained elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal
problems.why: Slightly loses the explicit comparison to the goal, though it follows.

A.summary: A lively level-4 retelling that keeps every decision and leaves the quotes intact; the best.

meaning.evidence: Mostly verbatim, but "voted unanimously to give a 1 the nod/4 percentage point increase" garbles the 1/4 point rise, and "its continuing swear blind to achieve" garbles resolve. A quoted statement is altered: "said righto to the following statement".

sense.evidence: "swear blind" (insist something is true) used as a noun for resolve; "give ... the nod" spliced through a fraction; "said righto" inside an official quotation.

authenticity.evidence: Mechanical splices no one would write: "give a 1 the nod/4 percentage point increase", "its continuing swear blind".

register.evidence: Largely untranslated apart from three broken swaps; far under level 4.

tone.evidence: Formal tone intact where untouched, broken by "said righto" in the Committee's own statement.

flow.evidence: Broken: "to give a 1 the nod/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate".

essence.evidence: Recognisably the minutes, with the credit-rate line no longer readable.

problems.quote: voted unanimously to give a 1 the nod/4 percentage point increase
problems.original: voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point increase
problems.why: Splits the fraction 1/4 and corrupts the rate change.

problems.quote: underlined its continuing swear blind to achieve
problems.original: underlined its continuing resolve to achieve
problems.why: Swear blind is a verb phrase meaning to insist; wrong sense and ungrammatical.

problems.quote: said righto to the following statement
problems.why: Alters text inside a quoted official statement.

problems.quote: Members noted that the unemployment rate was largely unchanged
problems.original: Members noted that the unemployment rate was largely unchanged
problems.why: Representative of the narrative left untranslated against a level-4 brief.

B.summary: Essentially untranslated, with broken swaps that corrupt a number and a quotation.

meaning.evidence: All decisions, rates, dates and votes kept, quotes intact: "lift the target range ... by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 per cent", "the unemployment rate had barely shifted", "help get inflation back ... sooner".

sense.evidence: Every term fits: "stuck with the FOMC's policy", "dead set on reaching", "Once the discussion wrapped up", "took in sign-off".

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian business English: "per cent", "dead set on", "wrapped up". Nothing forced.

register.evidence: Light for level 4: mostly plain rewording with a few touches ("dead set", "wrapped up", "stuck with").

tone.evidence: Keeps the sober minutes tone throughout.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "while inflation was still running above the Committee's 2 per cent goal".

variety.evidence: "wrapped up" twice ("Once the discussion wrapped up", "The meeting wrapped up"); otherwise little to repeat.

problems.quote: The meeting wrapped up at 10:15 a.m.
It was agreed that the Committee would next meet
problems.original: It was agreed that the next meeting of the Committee would be held
problems.why: Representative of how lightly the narrative is retold for a level-4 brief.

C.summary: Faithful and natural but lighter than the brief.
